text: A thin black cat starts following you home from school. It sits on the wall outside your window every night, watching.

choices.label: Take it in
choices.text: The cat moves into your room as if it always lived there. Somehow you sleep better.

choices.label: Follow it one night
choices.text: It leads you through alleys you never knew existed, then vanishes. You remember every turn.

text: You fall ill with a high fever that lasts a week. In your fever dreams you see a city on fire, and a figure in armor standing in the flames.
An older child decides you are an easy target and won't leave you alone.

choices.label: Fight back
choices.text: You lose the fight, but you never get picked on again.

choices.label: Talk your way out
choices.text: By the end of the month, the bully is somehow running errands for you.

choices.label: Outsmart them
choices.text: You work out their routine and simply make sure you are never where they are.

text: An old man feeding pigeons in the park tells you stories about a war between seven mages and seven ghosts of legend. He knows far too many details for a fairy tale.
Your parent takes you down into the workshop and shows you the family's Magic Crest: the stored work of generations, waiting to be passed on.

choices.label: Study it closely
choices.text: You spend months tracing every line of it in your mind.

choices.label: Ask what it cost
choices.text: Your parent is quiet for a long time, then tells you the family's real history.

text: The heads of several mage families gather to test the children of your generation.

choices.label: Show everything you can do
choices.text: They whisper about you afterwards. One of them leaves a card with an address on it.

choices.label: Hold back
choices.text: They dismiss you as average, which means nobody will see you coming.

text: In a moment of anger, every glass on the table shatters at once. Nobody can explain it. You think you can.
A woman who runs a herb shop notices the way lamps flicker around you. She says she was once a mage's apprentice, and offers to teach you what she knows.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: Her lessons are strange and unscientific, but they work.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: You decide not to trust her, and spend the time with your books instead.

text: You find your first real job. The pay is poor and the hours are long, but the money is yours.
A great-aunt you met only once dies and, to everyone's surprise, leaves something to you.
The whole city turns out for a festival. Lanterns, music and crowds fill the streets until dawn.

choices.label: Go with friends
choices.text: You meet half the city that night, it seems.

choices.label: Watch the crowd
choices.text: You notice a few people who seem to be watching the crowd too, and remember their faces.

text: You fall in love for the first time. It is wonderful for a while, and then it isn't.
A nervous antique dealer pulls you aside. He has something he wants to be rid of, and he thinks you are the sort of person who would want it.

choices.label: Buy it (50 money)
choices.text: He takes the money without counting it and hurries away.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: You will always wonder what it was.

text: Your family buys a radio. You sit in front of it every evening, listening to voices from cities you have never seen.
The first television set arrives on your street. Half the neighborhood crowds into one living room to watch it.
You get your hands on a secondhand home computer and teach yourself to program it from magazines.
You get your first smartphone. Suddenly you are in a dozen group chats at once.
A terrible influenza sweeps through {place}. Schools close, and there are funerals every day. You survive it, but you are never quite as strong again.
The Great War drags on. Men from your street leave for the front, and not all of them come back.
Night after night, the bombers come. You spend the nights in shelters and the mornings climbing over rubble.
Soldiers patrol the old town and people speak quietly in the streets. Your family learns to hide things, and so do you.
